name: Estonian Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Pärgma, J., Rathmann, C. & Herbszt-Romanek, P. Z. 2026. Estonian sign language research 1985–2024: a systematic literature review of methods, data, and research practices. Frontiers in Communication 11, doi:10.3389/fcomm.2026.1791199.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Survey of all 31 EVK studies 1985-2024 (Table 1); no work on stress or accent is listed; states that the lack of time-aligned annotation 'hinders systematic analysis of prosody, non-manuals'. Names the phonology works: Toom 1985/1988, Püvi 2006 BA thesis, Laiapea 2006 MA/2007 book, Toom et al. 2006, Paabo et al. 2009.

sources.citation: Pärgma, Jari. 2020. Küsimuse ja küsilause moodustamine eesti viipekeeles. MA thesis, University of Tartu. hdl:10062/68193.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 2.1 'Eesti viipekeele fonoloogia' (pp. 19–22) lists five phoneme classes (hand shape, place, movement, palm orientation, non-manual signals) after Toom et al. 2006; 'intonatsioon' used only for non-manual question marking; silent on word stress.

sources.citation: Paabo, Regina. 2012. Eesti viipekeel ja selle loome. Oma Keel 2012/2: 37–46.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 38 lists the sign phonemes (hand shape, location, movement, palm orientation, facial expression) and notes they are realised simultaneously; silent on stress/prosody.

sources.citation: Hollman, Liivi. 2010. Basic color terms in Estonian Sign Language. PhD dissertation, University of Tartu (Dissertationes linguisticae Universitatis Tartuensis 13). hdl:10062/14769.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 3.2 'ESL phonological system' (pp. 29–36) covers hand-form, location and movement inventories (36/23/29 in the Tartu 1989–90 system; 34/19/27 in Püvi 2006) and the 2006/2009 transcription systems; nothing on stress, accent or prosody. Notes the phoneme set 'definitely does not describe ESL phonological structure in full' (p. 36).

sources.citation: Paabo, Regina, Monika Födisch & Liivi Hollman. 2009. Rules for Estonian Sign Language transcription. Trames 13(63/58), 4: 401–424. doi:10.3176/tr.2009.4.05.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phoneme inventory (36 hand forms, 27 locations, 20 movements, orientation, two-hand relations) and glossing rules; 'stressed' occurs only in the sense 'emphasized' (reduplication gloss rule); silent on word stress.

sources.citation: Hollman, Liivi. 2006. Eesti kurtide kogukonnast ja eesti viipekeelest. Oma Keel 13 (2006/2): 36–44.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: pp. 40–41: phonological make-up = kireem counts (Porkuni 38 hand shapes; Tartu 36/23/29; 2005 study 34/19/27; 2006 transcription 38/26/26); grammar notes on time lines, tempo of verb signs for past tense, reduplication for duration; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Toom, Regina, Monika Trükmann & Liivi Hollman. 2006. Eesti viipekeele transkriptsioonist. Eesti Rakenduslingvistika Ühingu aastaraamat 2: 285–301. doi:10.5128/ERYa2.19.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Kireem (phoneme) inventory: 38 hand shapes, 26 locations, 26 movements, orientation symbols, non-manual glossing conventions (facial expressions for question types, negation etc.); 'rõhutatakse' appears only as 'is emphasized' in gloss rule 3 for repeated movement; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Laiapea, Vahur, Merilin Miljan, Regina Toom & Urmas Sutrop. 2002. Eesti viipekeele seisundikirjeldus. Tallinn: Eesti Keele Instituut. hdl:10062/40630.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Status report; one paragraph (pp. 6–7) on sign structure (four aspects: hand configuration, place, movement, palm orientation; non-manuals carry question/command); silent on stress.

sources.citation: Laiapea, Vahur. 2007. Keel on lahti: tähendusi viipekeelest. Tallinn: Eesti Keele Sihtasutus.

sources.note: General book-length overview of (Estonian) sign language by the founder of EVK research; cited by Paabo et al. 2009 as the general overview; could contain a prosody/emphasis remark.

sources.citation: Laiapea, Vahur. 2006. Tähendusi viipekeelest. MA thesis, University of Tartu.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Phonology/morphology description of EVK grammar per the 2026 review; not in Tartu DSpace.

sources.citation: Püvi, Egle. 2006. Eesti viipekeele kereoloogiasüsteemi kirjeldus. BA thesis, University of Tartu.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only systematic phonological description of EVK (383 signs, 80 phonemes) per Hollman 2010 and the 2026 review; the most likely place for any remark on prosodic/stress-like features, though probably parameter inventory only.
